passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Honeybees live in colonies.
• A worker bee that finds food returns to the hive.
• There, it performs a movement called the "waggle dance."
• The direction and length of the dance indicate the direction and distance of the food.
stem: The student wants to explain how honeybees share the location of food. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: A honeybee that finds food performs a "waggle dance" whose direction and length show other bees where the food is and how far away it is.
Honeybees live together in large colonies, and a worker bee that finds a source of food returns to the hive to share it with the colony.
When a worker honeybee finds food, it returns to its hive and performs a movement that beekeepers and scientists call the "waggle dance."
Honeybees live in colonies, and the worker bees in those colonies perform several different movements, including one called the waggle dance.
steps: The goal is to explain how bees share food locations.
A full explanation needs the dance and what the dance communicates.
Only one choice says the dance's direction and length show where the food is and how far away it is.
The other choices mention the hive or name the dance but never explain what information it carries.
key: "Explain how" needs the mechanism, not just the name of it.
